resale_co.name: Dwelling Certificate (Certificate of Inspection for 1 & 2 family dwellings, sale)
resale_co.issued_by: Clifton Fire Department, Fire Prevention Bureau, after Building, Tax and Zoning Department sign-off
resale_co.lead_time: Standard certificate: call the office 7 business days after the inspection; inspections are on Wednesdays 9am to 12 noon. Faster certificates cost more (within 4 to 20 days, or within 4 business days).
resale_co.valid_for: 6 months after the Fire Department inspection
requirements: No open permits on the property (Building Department check and stamp on the application)
Tax and Zoning Department approval (the Zoning Officer reviews and approves all Dwelling Certificates)
Smoke alarms on every level (basement, each floor), excluding crawl spaces and unfinished attics with pull-down stairs
Smoke alarm within 10 feet of the bedroom doors on any floor with bedrooms
All smoke alarms less than 10 years old; battery-only alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units; existing hardwired systems must be kept
Carbon monoxide alarms within 10 feet outside all sleeping areas, with more on each floor that has sleeping areas
Central station fire alarm must be tested beforehand by a Division of Fire Safety certified company; bring the test record or the inspection fails
Multiple sources of power label within 18 inches of the electrical panel and meter for homes with a generator, solar or battery storage (the Bureau supplies and installs the label at the inspection)
An adult over 18 must be present and all areas (unit, basement, attic, common areas) must be accessible

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Dwelling Smoke Detector and Carbon Monoxide Compliance completely (check Sale), signed by both seller and buyer. Call the Building Department (973-470-5809) to make sure there are no open permits and ask when and where to get the application stamped. Bring the stamped application, the fee (payable to the City of Clifton) and, if digital signatures are not verified, a copy of the sales contract to Clifton Fire Headquarters (Yellow House on the City Hall property, 900 Clifton Avenue). After-hours drop-off is available in the Fire Headquarters drop box. Certificates must be picked up in person.

resale_co.notes: Clifton's resale requirement is the Fire Prevention Bureau's Dwelling Certificate (Certificate of Inspection). The same certificate is the state smoke and carbon monoxide alarm certificate, and it is only issued after the Building (open permits), Tax and Zoning Departments sign off, so the fee is paid once; the fees are repeated under fire_cert. The packet (May 2025) also lists rental certificates at $75.00 per unit. Standard fees may be paid by personal check, money order, cashier's check, exact cash or credit card (transaction fee); expedited fees cannot be paid by personal check. Cash and card payments must be made in person; make payments to the City of Clifton. The City code (ecode360) could not be opened; web search summaries mention a different tiered fee schedule ($150 / $250 / $375) and a 180-day validity attributed to an ordinance, but no snippet showing exact Clifton code text was found, so those amounts are not used. The Building Department separately handles Certificates of Business Compliance for commercial sales. Rental dwellings also need a lead-based paint inspection (separate Lead Division program).

requirements: Smoke alarms on every level and within 10 feet of bedroom doors; all under 10 years old
Battery-only smoke alarms must be 10-year sealed battery units; existing hardwired systems must be maintained
CO alarms (UL 2034) within 10 feet outside all sleeping areas, on each floor with sleeping areas
Central station fire alarm test record from a Division of Fire Safety certified company is required at the inspection; inspectors will not test it
Multiple sources of power label for homes with a generator, solar or battery storage (supplied and installed by the Bureau at the inspection)

The City's Fire Department FAQ still says a dry chemical fire extinguisher, at least 10BC rated and no more than 10 pounds, is needed for the dwelling inspection; the May 2025 packet does not list one

fire_cert.notes: The Clifton Fire Department (Fire Prevention Bureau) is the fire code enforcing agency and issues the dwelling smoke and carbon monoxide certificate, which is also the City's resale Dwelling Certificate. The state directory lists Fire Official Michael Pressler (name misspelled 'Micahel' there) at (973) 470-5804; the City packet gives the office line (973) 470-5801, which is used here. The Fire Department FAQ still asks for a fire extinguisher at dwelling inspections although P.L.2025, c.19 removed it from the state sale certificate; confirm with the Bureau. Re-checked 2026-10-06: the Dwelling Application Packet is the same May 5, 2025 PDF with the same fees and phone numbers; the form header quote was split because the 'Sale / Rental' checkbox column sits between its lines in the PDF text.
